original_value: Covering a whole surface of a robot with tiny sensors which can measure local pressure and transmit the data through a network is an ideal solution to give an artificial skin to robots to improve a capability of action and safety. The crucial technological barrier is to package force sensor and communication function in a small volume. In this paper, we propose the novel device structure based on a wafer bonding technology to integrate and package capacitive force sensor using silicon diaphragm and an integrated circuit separately manufactured. Unique fabrication processes are developed, such as the feed-through forming using a dicing process, a planarization of the Benzocyclobutene (BCB) polymer filled in the feed-through and a wafer bonding to stack silicon diaphragm onto ASIC (application specific integrated circuit) wafer. The ASIC used in this paper has a capacitance measurement circuit and a digital communication interface mimicking a tactile receptor of a human. We successfully integrated the force sensor and the ASIC into a 2.5×2.5×0.3 mm die and confirmed autonomously transmitted packets which contain digital sensing data with the linear force sensitivity of 57,640 Hz/N and 10 mN of data fluctuation. A small stray capacitance of 1.33 pF is achieved by use of 10 μm thick BCB isolation layer and this minimum package structure.

result.paraphrase: A robot covered with tiny sensors that measure local pressure and send the data over a network would be an ideal artificial-skin solution for improving actuation capability and safety. The key technological challenge is packaging the force sensor and communication function within a compact volume. In this paper, we present a new device structure based on wafer bonding to integrate and package a capacitive force sensor with a silicon diaphragm and a separately fabricated integrated circuit. We developed unique fabrication steps, including feed-through formation by a dicing process, planarization of Benzocyclobutene (BCB) polymer filled into the feed-through, and wafer bonding to stack the silicon diaphragm onto an ASIC (application specific integrated circuit) wafer. The ASIC used here includes a capacitance measurement circuit and a digital communication interface that mimics a human tactile receptor. We successfully integrated the force sensor and ASIC into a 2.5×2.5×0.3 mm die and confirmed autonomous transmission of packets containing digital sensing data, with linear force sensitivity of 57,640 Hz/N and 10 mN data fluctuation. A low stray capacitance of 1.33 pF was achieved using a 10 μm-thick BCB isolation layer and this minimal package structure.
